english.title: Manufacturer fail to categorise a pyrotechnic article (not cat F1/F2/F3 firework) before placing on the market
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) was the manufacturer of a pyrotechnic article other than a category F1, F2 or F3 firework, namely **(..SPECIFY PYROTECHNIC ARTICLE..), and placed it on the market having failed to

(A)_[categorise it using the categories set out in Schedule 1 of the Pyrotechnic Articles (Safety) Regulations 2015, according to its type of use or purpose and level of hazard, including its noise level]_
(B)_[ensure that an approved body had confirmed its categorisation as part of a relevant conformity assessment procedure]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 6, 62(1)(a) and 63(2) of the Pyrotechnic Articles (Safety) Regulations 2015.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
being a manufacturer
before placing a pyrotechnic article on the market
failed to
categorise it / have its categorisation confirmed

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: The UK will continue to recognise the competency of EU based notified bodies to assess products to be placed on the UK market. Products that have been categorised by an EU a notified body rather will be covered under the remit of 'approved bodies' for the purposes of legislation and items already categorised by such bodies will not need re-assessment before being placed on the UK market.

other.penalty:
Summary: Three months imprisonment and/or a fine
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine

None
